original_question: For the generalized pentagram maps T_{I,J} on twisted polygons in projective space, is every map T_{I,I} integrable for every multi-index I?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 6.3 in §6: whether the generalized single-polygon pentagram maps T_{I,I} (that is, the case I = J inside Definition 1.5) are integrable. This is narrower than the broader §4 discussion of universal pentagram maps. ([math.utoronto.ca](https://www.math.utoronto.ca/khesin/papers/nonintegrability9.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper’s main target almost exactly: it uses the notation T_{I,J}, singles out the diagonal case J = I, and asks for integrability for all such choices of I, which is essentially the content of Conjecture 6.3. ([math.utoronto.ca](https://www.math.utoronto.ca/khesin/papers/nonintegrability9.pdf))
missing_details: It should specify that I is a (d-1)-tuple of integers for some ambient dimension d ≥ 2; in the paper, the length of I determines the projective dimension. ([math.utoronto.ca](https://www.math.utoronto.ca/khesin/papers/nonintegrability9.pdf))

A fully stand-alone version should define the generalized map itself: P_k^I := (v_k, v_{k+i_1}, ..., v_{k+i_1+...+i_{d-1}}), and T_{I,J}v_k := P_k^I ∩ P_{k+j_1}^I ∩ ... ∩ P_{k+j_1+...+j_{d-1}}^I. ([math.utoronto.ca](https://www.math.utoronto.ca/khesin/papers/nonintegrability9.pdf))

It should identify the phase space: projective equivalence classes P_n of generic twisted n-gons in P^d, where v_{k+n} = M∘v_k for some monodromy M ∈ SL_{d+1}, and no d+1 consecutive vertices lie in one hyperplane. ([math.utoronto.ca](https://www.math.utoronto.ca/khesin/papers/nonintegrability9.pdf))

It should make explicit the quantifier in n: the conjecture is posed for pentagram maps on twisted n-gons without fixing n, so the natural stand-alone reading is for every n for which the map is generically defined. ([math.utoronto.ca](https://www.math.utoronto.ca/khesin/papers/nonintegrability9.pdf))

Because the map is defined by intersecting hyperplanes, the refined question should implicitly restrict to the generic locus where those intersections exist and define a rational self-map of P_n. ([math.utoronto.ca](https://www.math.utoronto.ca/khesin/papers/nonintegrability9.pdf))

If one wants full self-containment, the ambient field should be pinned down: the paper says the definitions work over any base field, while R, C, and Q are used for visualization, algebraic-geometric integrability, and arithmetic experiments, respectively. ([math.utoronto.ca](https://www.math.utoronto.ca/khesin/papers/nonintegrability9.pdf))

The exact meaning of integrable is left implicit in Conjecture 6.3; nearby, Theorem 1.4 treats integrable pentagram maps via Lax representations with a spectral parameter, and §3 also introduces a generalized discrete-integrability notion allowing jumps between invariant tori. ([math.utoronto.ca](https://www.math.utoronto.ca/khesin/papers/nonintegrability9.pdf))

To remain paper-faithful, it should be clear that the conjecture concerns the generalized maps T_{I,J} of Definition 1.5, not the broader universal pentagram maps introduced in §4. ([math.utoronto.ca](https://www.math.utoronto.ca/khesin/papers/nonintegrability9.pdf))
refined_question: For each d ≥ 2, each n, and each tuple I = (i_1, ..., i_{d-1}) ∈ Z^{d-1}, let P_n denote the space of projective-equivalence classes of generic twisted n-gons (v_k) in CP^d, where v_{k+n} = M∘v_k for some M ∈ SL_{d+1}(C). Define the diagonal hyperplanes P_k^I := (v_k, v_{k+i_1}, ..., v_{k+i_1+...+i_{d-1}}), and define the generalized pentagram map T_{I,I} by T_{I,I}v_k := P_k^I ∩ P_{k+i_1}^I ∩ ... ∩ P_{k+i_1+...+i_{d-1}}^I whenever this intersection is generically defined. Is every such map T_{I,I}: P_n → P_n integrable, in the same sense as the integrable pentagram maps treated in Theorem 1.4? ([math.utoronto.ca](https://www.math.utoronto.ca/khesin/papers/nonintegrability9.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, by the duality T_{I,J}^{-1} = T_{J^*,I^*} ∘ Sh from equation (1.2), one may ask the same question with I replaced by its reversed tuple I^*, since T_{I,I} and T_{I^*,I^*} are integrable or non-integrable simultaneously. ([math.utoronto.ca](https://www.math.utoronto.ca/khesin/papers/nonintegrability9.pdf))
justification: The draft is aiming at the exact conjecture stated in §6, not at the broader necessary-condition conjecture for universal pentagram maps in §4. The notation and scope come from Definition 1.5 and Definition 1.1, while Remark 6.2 and the table on pp. 12–13 give the immediate context: several 3D examples with I = J show moderate height growth, and these observations are then distilled into Conjecture 6.3. Theorem 1.4 supplies the nearby benchmark family of already-proved integrable pentagram maps used as the comparison class for the word integrable. ([math.utoronto.ca](https://www.math.utoronto.ca/khesin/papers/nonintegrability9.pdf))
